item.title: IPL 2027 Retention List: When and where to watch today's announcements; check date, time and live streaming details
item.description: The wait is almost over for IPL fans, with all 10 franchises set to submit their list of retained and released players for the 2027 season on Tuesday, November 17. The original deadline was November 15, but the BCCI extended it by two days. The change reportedly came because the earlier date coincided with the fifth and final ODI between India and New Zealand. With several big player trades already completed, the retention announcements are expected to bring more clarity on the squads ahead of the IPL 2027 mini-auction. IPL 2027 retention list: Deadline All 10 franchises must submit their list of retained and released players to the BCCI by Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The teams will reveal which players they want to keep for the next season and which ones they have decided to release. Players released by their franchises will become part of the auction pool. What time will the IPL 2027 retention list be announced? The BCCI and the official broadcaster have not confirmed the exact announcement time. However, reports suggest that the programme will begin at 5:40 PM IST. The announcements are expected to take place in the evening, following the trend from previous seasons. Where to watch IPL 2027 retention list live? Fans can watch the IPL 2027 retention announcements live on the Star Sports Network. The live stream will be available on the JioHotstar app and website in India. What is the IPL retention list? Before every IPL auction, all 10 franchises submit the names of players they want to retain and those they wish to release. Retained players remain with their respective teams for the upcoming season, while released players enter the auction pool and can be picked by any franchise. The rules for retaining players depend on the type of auction. Ahead of a mega auction, franchises have to follow a fixed limit on the number of players they can retain. However, there is no fixed retention limit ahead of a mini-auction. There will be no mega auction before IPL 2027. The teams will instead prepare for a mini-auction, which is scheduled to take place in Goa on December 16, 2026. IPL 2027 Retention: How many players can IPL teams retain? There is no fixed limit on the number of players a franchise can retain ahead of a mini-auction. However, teams must follow the squad-size rules. Each franchise can have a maximum of 25 players, including no more than eight overseas players. What is the IPL 2027 salary cap? The total salary cap for each franchise for IPL 2027 is Rs 157 crore. The amount spent on retained players will be deducted from the total purse. The remaining amount will be available to the franchise at the mini-auction. IPL 2027 mini-auction: Date and venue The IPL 2027 mini-auction will be held in Goa on December 16, 2026. Since this is a mini-auction, teams will have the opportunity to strengthen their squads by signing players released by other franchises and those who enter the auction pool. item.title: Thomas Frank explains why Crystal Palace job was ‘too good to turn down’
item.description: Thomas Frank decided the Crystal Palace job was “too good to turn down” after talks with chairman Steve Parish. The 53-year-old Dane, out of work since being sacked by Tottenham in February, has spent the last nine months travelling, spending time with family, and reflecting on his career. He takes charge of what he believes is an “iconic” English club , but one with plenty of work to do if they want to escape the Premier League relegation battle. “You know, honestly speaking, I was a little bit, ‘When do I want to go back in? Is it now?’ Then this opportunity came up,” Frank told PalaceTV. “I was thinking, this is probably too good to turn down for various reasons.” Frank’s strong admiration for Eagles supporters – he was at Wembley when Palace lifted the FA Cup – was a contributing factor. He added: “The second part of it was the very good conversation with Steve Parish. He’s been around, he knows what’s happening, he knows how to run a football club. “You always say you need to do your due diligence about the one who takes the decisions, and everything I’ve heard about Steve, everything I knew, it was positive, and then on top of that the conversation with Matt Hobbs, Iain Moody, was big. “So all that adding up, looking into the team that I see is extremely exciting, good potential, or just thinking, ‘Hmm, this is interesting’. And when I’m sitting here, walking around the training ground, it was just, ‘Ok, you’re back’, which scared me a little bit, but it’s good.” That Hobbs and Moody helped convince Frank to sign a two-and-a-half year deal will, for Palace fans, carry hope that the new boss will be backed in the January transfer window. The Eagles lost a number of key personnel in the summer from their Conference League-winning squad, including Daniel Munoz to Nottingham Forest and Maxence Lacroix to Chelsea. Thomas Frank arrives with Palace in the relegation zone (Reuters) Their absence has been felt on a side that has conceded the most goals, 24, in the Premier League. “To state the obvious, we need to stabilise things,” said Frank, who pointed to defending, set pieces in both boxes, and defensive transitions as priorities to address, beginning with Saturday’s trip to Coventry. “We need to bring energy, we need to bring belief, we need to bring confidence, because this is a very, very good team with very good players, but they need to believe in themselves. “We need to balance a lot of things with aiming high in Europe, two fantastic cup tournaments, but of course the Premier League is the most important if we need to prioritise, but we would like to compete in all things.” Frank, who was sacked by Tottenham after a run of only two wins in 17 matches, said he needed to “re-energise” after that disappointment. Hamilton's Ravens dropped to 4-6 as a result of the 23-20 setback Monday in Baltimore. The Ravens, who went 4-1 to start the season, head into a two-game road trip with a five-game losing streak. item.title: 'I've heard': What Bam Adebayo has done behind the scenes to 'make it work' with Giannis Antetokounmpo
item.description: Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images The Miami Heat are looking like a more complete team again after their terrible start to the season. The Heat lost each of their first four games of the campaign and were viewed by many as the worst team in the division at that stage. Since then, they have won eight of their 10 games and are now looking brilliant. Giannis Antetokounmpo has been consistently brilliant, but the one player who has recently stepped up is Bam Adebayo. Bam Adebayo sought help to ‘make it work’ with Giannis Antetokounmpo Adebayo had his struggles early on in the season. Everyone knows how good a player the 29-year-old can be, but there were times when he just didn’t look like his usual aggressive self. That led to a lot of criticism, with people like Michael Beasley claiming that Adebayo looks like he doesn’t even want to be there anymore. However, in the recent games against the Pistons and the Cavaliers, Adebayo came up with a combined 57 points, 19 rebounds and seven assists. His partnership with Antetokounmpo looks a lot better now, and Marc J. Spears has revealed one of the reasons why. Adebayo apparently reached out to people behind the scenes to figure out how to play with the Greek superstar and succeed alongside him. Spears said on ESPN: “Bam and Klay were both saying, ‘This is a work in progress. Be patient.’ “I’ve heard that Bam has kind of reached out to people, trying to figure out ways, showing some leadership and trying to work with Giannis. “Remember the Heatles were like 10-8 – they started off this way, this is the new Heatles, you could say. They are a work in progress, and it’s going great now. “They are 7-2 off late, they are winning, and these guys are figuring it out. And I think they’re going to get better and better and better. “So, shoutout to Bam for trying to figure out a way to make it work.” Adebayo was in action for the Heat in their most recent game against the Houston Rockets. He played 16 minutes, scored four points and recorded one rebound, two assists and two steals. However, a right hip problem ruled him out of the rest of the game, which was a real shame, just as he was starting to look like his usual self again. Thankfully, though, coach Erik Spoelstra revealed after the game that he does not expect Adebayo to be sidelined long-term.

item.title: Jurgen Klopp reveals he tried to sign Marc-Andre ter Stegen for Liverpool: ‘But he preferred Barcelona’
item.description: Jurgen Klopp reveals he tried to sign Marc-Andre ter Stegen for Liverpool: ‘But he preferred Barcelona’ Having served as Barcelona’s first-choice goalkeeper for years, Marc-Andre ter Stegen faced a perennial battle with Manuel Neuer in the national team setup and never found himself well poised to be Germany’s starting goalkeeper. For years, the opportunity continually evaded him, to the point where it appeared he may well complete his career without enjoying the honour of being his country’s starting goalkeeper. Now, on loan at Ajax from Barcelona , he is finally enjoying his time as a regular starter for Germany and has been doing well for both club and country after what was a difficult period for him. Last night, he played all ninety minutes in their rout over Xavi’s Netherlands. Klopp speaks on Ter Stegen Manager of the German national team, Jurgen Klopp, spoke to the media about the goalkeeper after his team’s demolition of the Netherlands and heaped praise on Ter Stegen. Klopp tried to sign Ter Stegen at Liverpool. (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) In what came as a surprising development, he admitted to being interested in signing the Barcelona goalkeeper when he was the manager of Liverpool. “I have always considered him an exceptional goalkeeper and I wanted to bring him to Liverpool, but he preferred Barcelona,” he said, as quoted by Mundo Deportivo . Klopp then went on with his usual humour, stating that he did not have any hard feelings against Ter Stegen for rejecting his approach. “I don’t hold a grudge against him.” What’s next for Ter Stegen? Slowly reviving his career. (Photo by Alex Caparros/Getty Images) While Ter Stegen’s loan at Ajax is only until 2027, Barcelona likely do not have him in their plans for the future. Joan Garcia, after all, has established himself as the No. 1 starter in goal at Barça and Dominik Livakovic stands as a more than able deputy to the Spaniard. The real purpose behind Barcelona loaning their former captain, quite clearly, was to help him make his name in Europe once more – something he has done well over the past few months. Needless to say, their idea will be to part ways with him in the summer, possibly to make some profit and primarily to clear their wage bill given how finance remains one of their primary areas of concern.

item.title: JJ Gabriel fee revealed! Real Madrid set to pay Manchester United nominal compensation for teenage sensation as contract details emerge
item.description: JJ Gabriel - Getty Images Real Madrid are on the verge of completing a sensational swoop for Manchester United prodigy JJ Gabriel as the financial details of the deal begin to emerge. The teenage sensation is expected to formalise his move to the Spanish capital within days, marking the end of a long-running transfer saga. Madrid finalise three-year deal and €360,000 fee Gabriel's new agent, Ali Barat, visited Valdebebas on Monday to iron out the final terms of the agreement, according to journalist Pablo Gallego . The 16-year-old is now expected to put pen to paper before the end of the week. Per El Chiringuito TV reporter Marcos Benito, the English youngster will sign a three-year contract with Los Blancos . Real Madrid will pay Manchester United a nominal €360,000 fee in training compensation to secure his signature. Behind the Old Trafford exit and rejected peace talks The transfer follows a breakdown in Manchester that began when Gabriel walked away from the club in September . He has not trained with the Premier League giants since his departure. Dissatisfied with United's plans for his first-team integration , the teenager asked the club to cancel his registration. The Red Devils rejected that request and later attempted to reconcile, only for their efforts to go unanswered by Gabriel and his camp. Why the real cost dwarfs the nominal compensation While the €360,000 compensation figure appears modest for one of England's brightest young talents, Real Madrid's total financial outlay will be far higher. Once the player's salary, agent fees, and commissions are factored in, the overall operation could cost between €10–15 million. Securing the wonderkid also marks a major recruitment win for the Spanish club. Gabriel turned down serious interest from Paris Saint-Germain, Bayern Munich, and Barcelona in order to make the move to Madrid. item.description: Andorra owner Gerard Pique believes that goalkeeper Jesus Owono does not deserve the 12-match ban he received following the death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel . Owono collided with De Miguel in stoppage time of a Spanish second-tier match on 2 November, with De Miguel subsequently rushed to intensive care before passing away the morning after in hospital. Owono, who was sent off for the foul before the match was abandoned, said he was going through “the most difficult days of my life” in the aftermath of De Miguel’s death. He has since been hit with a lengthy suspension for violent conduct by the Spanish football federation (Rfef), with its disciplinary committee saying he used “excessive force” in the collision. Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban after the death of Jesus de Miguel (AP) This has drawn the ire of former Barcelona defender Pique, the majority shareholder of Owono’s club Andorra, who feels the Equatorial Guinea stopper is being punished for the consequences rather than his action. "Players, ​former ⁠players, coaches, goalkeepers, everyone has called it an accident," Pique said in a video posted on social media ⁠late on Monday. “I truly believe that imposing the maximum sanction on Jesus for this action puts him in a situation he does not deserve, because he is not to blame for all of this having happened.” Pique says there is inconsistency in the punishment, citing Albacete winger Jose Corpas’ three-match ban after his high challenge on Sabadell midfielder Quadri Liameed left him hospitalised. Gerard Pique is the owner of second-tier club Andorra (AFP/Getty) “Fortunately Quadri is fine, the consequences in this case were not fatal, and the committee decided to sanction Corpas with three matches,” he added. “With all this, my reflection is: what is being sanctioned, the action or the consequences?” Andorra general manager Jaume Nogues told Andorra Radio and Television on Tuesday that they would not be appealing the disciplinary committee's decision, but that their resolution on the case was "not done well". Nogues said an appeal would be "frowned upon socially", adding that Owono was also not in favour of launching an appeal. Meanwhile, Tenerife manager Alvaro Cervera ‌did not agree with Pique's evaluation. item.description: Deshaun Watson © Reuters Deshaun Watson has been one of the NFL’s most criticized players since being traded to the Cleveland Browns in 2022. That said, he may be on track to rehabilitate his image this year. On Sunday against the Houston Texans, the Cleveland Browns quarterback underperformed in the air, not throwing a single touchdown and being intercepted once. However, he was also one of three players who had a rushing touchdown in the 27-24 victory, which ended a two-game skid. That performance prompted high praise from ESPN’s Stephen A. He named Watson his choice for Comeback Player of the Year, notably passing over Patrick Mahomes in the process: “Patrick Mahomes is not the Comeback Player of the Year. … They really thought this guy, who was an all-pro player, was going to give up and roll over into a ball, and he couldn’t play anymore. …They mocked me for saying he could still play! item.description: A fan who racially abused Kylian Mbappe during a LaLiga match last year has been handed an 11-month suspended prison sentence after being convicted of a hate crime. The suspension of the sentence is conditional on the unnamed fan not attending football stadiums for any official sports competitions for two years. The individual has also been handed a fine along with “various disqualification penalties”, Real Madrid said in a statement. “This ruling adds to the criminal convictions already issued for racist insults against Real Madrid players at the Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas, and José Zorrilla stadiums,” the club statement continued. “Real Madrid, which has acted as a private prosecutor in this case and continues to do so in others involving similar incidents, reaffirms its commitment to combating racism and eradicating any racist behavior in football and sports.” Kylian Mbappe suffered the abuse during last year's meeting between Real Madrid and Real Oviedo (Getty) The incident occurred during Real Madrid’s 3-0 win over Real Oviedo at the Carlos Tartiere Stadium in August 2025, during which Mbappe bagged a brace. Vinicius Jr , who has been persistently targeted with racist abuse at multiple stadiums in Spain as well as online, also scored in the match. After the match, LaLiga reported alleged racist chanting towards Mbappe and Vinicius to Spain’s National Police, with the league alleging that chants imitating monkey sounds were heard on multiple occasions. In March 2024, Vinicius broke down in tears during an emotional press conference as he bemoaned that racism was getting worse as perpetrators were going unpunished. “I just want to play football but it’s hard to move forward… I feel less and less like playing (due to the racist abuse),” he said.

In the article, Petriello cites three specific issues with having a permanent DH that is named Ohtani, and their current roster construction – having the oldest corner infielders in the league, their best rising star is also a DH, and that Dalton Rushing isn’t ready to catch again yet but can hit. Petriello says there are two things that the Dodgers could do about it – Let Josue De Paula play left field, and move Tommy Edman back to a utility player role, spelling those aging players. Petriello also notes that this is most likely the last season the Dodgers would have to deal with the current makeup of the team, as both Max Muncy and Freddie Freeman’s contracts will be up at the end of the 2027 season. If there’s any team that can be creative with their roster, we know it will be the Dodgers. Jack Harris of the California Post posits that the Dodgers will not be offering Tarik Skubal a big long-term contract, as they have to many big-name free agents in the past, but should instead work on convincing the two-time Cy Young winner a higher, but shorter term contract. CBS Sports’s Brad Crawford wrote that the time for Reed as the starter is over. The Case for a Change at Quarterback Third-year coach Mike Elko faces pressure to fix the offense. item.title: Springboks supremo Rassie Erasmus has gone too far and his latest rant puts rugby in danger
item.description: Time spent in the company of Rassie Erasmus is rarely boring. The all-powerful Springboks supremo often speaks as almost a stream of consciousness, the undiluted thoughts of a most active and sometimes brilliant mind. When World Rugby gathers some of the sport’s power-brokers to discuss points of law, or the shape of the game, it is said to be the South Africa head coach who most often holds the room with that strange, beguiling charisma he carries. On Monday afternoon, though, Erasmus went too far – again. In a 25-minute press conference ostensibly to talk about his team selection for the game , the 54-year-old took aim at what he perceives as a number of recent injustices within the sport, all of which have worked against his team. There was a dangerous tackle from Ireland fly half Sam Prendergast against Fiji, which went unpunished but has since been cited. There were the 16 or 17 – Erasmus used both figures – “knee-drop” tackles made by France in the Springboks’ 21-19 defeat in Paris on Friday night . There was the claim that Maxime Lucu had returned from the sin bin before a full 10 minutes had elapsed in that game. It was pointed out that the Ireland prop Tadhg Furlong was cleared by a disciplinary panel off an alleged groin grab of an opponent when South Africa hooker Jan-Hendrik Wessels had served a ban under the same charge last year. South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus has risked the wrath of World Rugby (PA Wire) One could, to some extent, understand each of the points that Erasmus was making. It was slightly strange that Prendergast’s tackle was missed by the matchday officials given the detailed study of “hip-drop” tackles that had preceded this campaign – though there is plenty for television match officials to monitor. That it has been cited, though, represents good process; a red-card offence may not have been picked up on the game but could meet subsequent punishment. With France clearly intent on tackling low , Eramsus is right that a few knee-drop tackles may have been missed. Siya Kolisi, the South Africa captain, could be heard pointing out as much to referee Andrea Piardi during the Stade de France thriller. But one must be cautious not to re-litigate each and every moment of a Test. Were referees to officiate strictly to the law-book, the game would become even more stilted and stop-start. There is always a balance to be struck in terms of continuity and materiality. Siya Kolisi expressed frustration during South Africa's defeat to France (Getty) And that was where Erasmus slipped up. Rather than fully acknowledging the difficult role the officials have, he suggested something more insidious. Tangled in a web of thoughts both convergent and divergent, Erasmus appeared to intimate that officials may have been “match-fixing”. While he later insisted that it was “not an accusation”, and that he had not been talking about his team, it was a slip that may well drawn punishment from World Rugby. item.title: DeChambeau and Rahm join DP World Tour after LIV Golf collapse
item.description: FILE PHOTO - US golfer Bryson DeChambeau tees off the 10th during day three of The 154th Open Championship at Royal Birkdale in Southport. (is associated with: «DeChambeau and Rahm join DP World Tour after LIV Golf collapse») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm have both been confirmed on the DP World Tour for 2027 following the collapse of LIV Golf. DeChambeau joins as member of the DP World Tour for the first time in Category 1 status, which has been activated under a five-year exemption he received after winning the 2024 US Open and was reportedly lodged before Sunday’s application deadline. The US star's inclusion could eventually offer him a route to regaining his US PGA Tour card for 2028. The US PGA is taking a harder stance against ex-LIV players returning. Former major champions Dustin Johnson, Cameron Smith and Bubba Watson will also feature on the DP World Tour next year, having signed agreements to receive invites to a “specific number of tournaments.” At the start of November LIV Golf announced it intends to “transition to an orderly wind-down of its operations,” bringing an end to the controversial breakaway tour. It had been reported BC Partners Credit, who had been lined up as potential backers following the withdrawal of Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund, had pulled out of a deal due to an exodus of star players. LIV, which launched in 2022, was forced to apply for chapter 11 bankruptcy in the US, effectively cancelling playing contracts. Former Masters champions Sergio Garcia and Patrick Reed – who left LIV Golf ahead of the 2026 season and has since earned back his PGA Tour card – have also been confirmed among the 22 ex-major champions in exempt membership on the DP World Tour (formerly European Tour) for 2027. DP World Tour’s chief executive Guy Kinnings expects the 2027 season to be “one of the most keenly contested campaigns in our 55-year history.” Kinnings said in a statement: “There has been significant change in the landscape of men’s professional golf over the past 12 months. As golf’s global tour, we have taken a pragmatic approach to this unique and unprecedented situation as we go into next year, always with the best interests of our entire membership at the forefront of our minds. “We realize there are different viewpoints, but this approach, discussed and agreed with our Tournament Committee and allied to this responsibly managed programme of invites, will add value which, in turn, will benefit the Tour as a whole.”

item.title: New Zealand handed huge injury boost with Will Jordan in line to face England
item.description: Will Jordan will recover from a torn hamstring in time for Saturday’s Nations Championship match against England. Jordan, the most prolific finisher in All Blacks history with 56 tries in 64 Tests, was in danger of missing the rest of the tour because of the injury sustained against Scotland on 7 November. But attack coach Mike Blair revealed the 28-year-old wing’s progress has been encouraging ahead of Thursday’s team announcement. “Will did a fair bit of training today,” former Scotland scrum-half Blair said on Tuesday. “He’s ahead of schedule where we thought he would be and we’ll make a decision on him over the next couple of days, but he had a good run around today.” New Zealand are still reeling from their shock 35-28 defeat by Wales – one of the greatest upsets of all time – and are promising a backlash at Allianz Stadium in their last outing before finals weekend. “Horrible result,” Blair said. “It’s been a really quiet changing room over the last couple of days. “We’ve been reflecting from a team point of view and I’ve been reflecting from my point of view, looking at what I could have done differently, what we could have done better. “The great thing is we’ve got a game this weekend. We’ve had a chat about where we can improve, what we can do better and these guys are going to be firing when we come out against England on Saturday. “Credit to Wales as well. item.title: Fantasy football keep, drop, trade, Week 11: What to do with Tyler Warren, Panthers WRs?
item.description: 10 weeks down. Four to go. The sprint to the fantasy football playoffs has begun. That means tough decisions need to be made for rosters ravaged by injuries or sitting on their league's cut line. Underperforming stars have to be sent to the bench or worse. Inconsistent sleepers may not produce the juice needed to justify a squeeze. As margins for error narrow, success and regret even out the scales of fantasy justice. Let's see if we can't tilt them closer to the former. Keep, drop or trade is our weekly breakdown of the underperforming studs and overperforming sleepers who could be in for a sudden momentum change that could sink fantasy rosters or carry them to pretend sports Valhalla. I'm joined by our resident fantasy expert and Rhode Island Scumbag Mike "Yaj" Boyajian to talk about six players who might have you cursing projected point totals on a weekly basis. Who should you keep? Who should you bench? And who should you trade or drop as the actual NFL season crashes into its back nine? Hopefully we can clear things up for you. WR Tetairoa McMillan, Carolina Panthers Christian: Hold and start . If only to avoid the hindsight embarrassment of missing out on a 40-point explosion in favor of a seven-point day from someone like Tank Dell. McMillan is still getting red zone and end zone targets, even if they’re coming much less frequently.
